statement: Build a one-page website for Brew Lab, a small specialty coffee shop in Indiranagar, Bengaluru, whose main job is to get a phone visitor to a pre-order for pickup in as few taps as possible. The page also shows the menu with prices, opening hours and location, with a compact beans and farms section and a compact loyalty-card explainer (buy 9, get the 10th free) below the order flow.
audience: Phone visitors in and around Indiranagar, Bengaluru who want to see the menu and pre-order a coffee for pickup.
standards: Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file, no build step; CDN libraries are allowed.
Mobile-first and usable on a phone.
Warm and modern look, delivered through visual design rather than long story sections.
No invented facts: anything only the shop owner knows appears as a visibly marked placeholder.
rules: Pre-order has no server and no payment: the form builds a pre-filled order message and opens WhatsApp, with email as fallback, and payment is at pickup.
The order flow comes before the beans and farms and loyalty sections.
Do not invent farm names or sourcing claims.
Menu items and prices, opening hours, address, WhatsApp number and farm details are marked placeholders on the page.
The beans and farms section and the loyalty explainer stay compact; the accepted trade-off is less room for brand story.
done_when: The site is a single HTML file with its CSS and JavaScript inline, needing no build step.
The file has a viewport meta tag and responsive CSS, and the main buttons and form controls are at least 44px tall.
A visible Pre-order button or link in the header or first section scrolls to or opens the order form.
In the file's source order, the order form and menu come before the beans and farms section and the loyalty section.
The menu lists each item with a price shown in rupees.
The page has an opening hours section and a location section naming Indiranagar, Bengaluru.
The order form lets the visitor pick items from the menu, enter a name and a pickup time, and states that payment is at pickup.

The form's JavaScript builds a pre-filled order message and opens a WhatsApp link (wa.me) with a mailto link as fallback, and the page has no payment fields and no on-screen text claiming the order was placed.
A beans and farms section exists and contains no farm name or sourcing claim that is not marked as a placeholder.
A loyalty-card section states: buy 9, get the 10th free.
Every placeholder value (menu items and prices, hours, address, WhatsApp number, email, farm details) carries a visible on-page placeholder marker, and the file contains no unmarked invented facts.
CSS variables define a warm colour palette that the page uses for backgrounds, text and buttons.
open_inputs: Shop email address for the fallback
Farm names and sourcing details for the beans and farms section
Pickup time rules (for example, minimum lead time)
